item.title: Health PEI Board announces new CEO
item.description:
Health PEI Board announces new CEO jenniferdhogan Wed, 10/28/2026 - 16:29

The Health PEI Board of Directors has appointed Laurae Kloschinsky as Chief Executive Officer of Health PEI, effective immediately, following a competitive recruitment process.

Kloschinsky has served as Interim Chief Executive Officer since March 2026, providing stable leadership during a period of significant healthcare transformation. She brings extensive leadership experience and has worked closely with health care providers, communities, government and system partners to advance innovation and improve access to care for Islanders.

"Since stepping into the interim role, Laurae has provided steady leadership, a strong focus on patients and staff, and a commitment to collaboration with health care professionals, government, communities and system partners across Prince Edward Island," said Dr. Wedge. "The Board is confident her experience, vision and ability to build strong partnerships will help Health PEI continue improving access to care and strengthening services for Islanders."

As Chief Executive Officer, Kloschinsky will lead Health PEI in delivering health care services across the province while advancing organizational priorities focused on Right People, Right Care, Right Place and Right Time.

"Laurae has built strong relationships with health care professionals, community partners and stakeholders across Prince Edward Island. Her appointment provides leadership continuity as we continue working together to improve access to care and strengthen our healthcare system for Islanders."

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

"It is a privilege to lead Health PEI and work alongside dedicated physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, allied health professionals, staff, volunteers and partners who support healthcare delivery across our province," said Laurae Klonchinsky. "Together, we will continue focusing on providing high-quality care, supporting our workforce, and ensuring Islanders receive the care they need, when and where they need it."

Kloschinsky is an experienced health care executive and pharmacist from rural PEI, with extensive experience in health care operations, change management, communications, technology implementation, and system innovation. Prior to her appointment as Interim Chief Executive Officer, she held senior leadership roles within the Government of PEI and worked closely with health care partners across Prince Edward Island to advance improvements in health care delivery.

item.title: Pharmacy Plus PEI marks four-year anniversary
item.description:
Pharmacy Plus PEI marks four-year anniversary jenniferdhogan Wed, 10/28/2026 - 10:23

This month marks the fourth anniversary of Pharmacy Plus PEI, with more than 91, 800 Islanders having accessed over 309,500 assessments since the program began.

The Pharmacy Plus PEI program supports 48 participating pharmacies in 15 communities across the province to renew eligible prescriptions and assess and prescribe for 35 common ailments and conditions. 

“Every day, Islanders are receiving timely care close to home through Pharmacy Plus PEI.  Since its inception, more than $6.67 million worth of direct patient care has been provided through the program.  I want to thank pharmacists across the Island for the important service they provide in their communities. Their dedication to patient care has made this program a success.”

- Minister of Health and Wellness Cory Deagle

Since its launch, participating pharmacies have provided a range of assessment and prescribing services including the following (as of Oct. 15, 2026):  

  • Over 197,360 prescription renewal assessments (63.8 per cent of all Pharmacy Plus assessments)
  • Over 21,800 urinary tract infection assessments (7 per cent)
  • Over 9,400 allergic rhinitis assessments (3 per cent)
  • Over 7,400 cough assessments (2.4 per cent)
  • Over 5,800 nasal congestion assessments (1.87 per cent)
  • Over 1,400 contraception assessments (since the service expanded in July 2023)

The program also expanded in December 2025 to include strep throat testing and treatment as part of sore throat assessments. More than 2,900 Islanders have accessed the service to date, helping divert patients from emergency departments and other primary health care settings.

“The Pharmacy Plus Program has demonstrated that an investment in pharmacy services results in increased access to health care,” said PEI Pharmacy Association executive director Erin MacKenzie. “We look forward to ongoing conversations, focused on expanding our scope of care through sustainable models that protect and enhance patient access”.

For more information, visit Pharmacy Plus PEI

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
